verb:entgegenkommen.tx: From Middle High German engegenkomen, ingagenkomen, from Old High German ingeginqueman, ingeginiqueman, ingagankweman. Equivalent to entgegen- + kommen.

verb:ermuntern.tx: From Middle High German ermuntern, ermundern, from Old High German irmuntaren. Equivalent to er- + munter + -en.

phrase:Ehre, wem Ehre gebührt.tx: Literally, “honour to whom honour is due”.

verb:einleuchten.tx: Inherited from Middle High German īnliuhten, Old High German inliuhtan; by surface analysis, ein + leuchten.

verb:exhumieren.tx: Borrowed from Medieval Latin exhumō, from Latin ex- + humō (“to bury”), + -ieren.

verb:entweihen.tx: From Middle High German entwīhen. Equivalent to ent- + weihen.

verb:erblicken.tx: From Middle High German erblicken, from Old High German irblikken. Equivalent to er- + blicken.

verb:entlieben.tx: From ent- (“un-, dis-”) + lieben (“to love”). Attested since at least the 17th century, but usually in translation or as an ad-hoc antonym of verlieben. Not in the older dictionaries. Somewhat more regular use seems to begin only in the later 20th century.

verb:erblühen.tx: From Middle High German erblüejen, from Old High German irbluoen. Equivalent to er- + blühen.

verb:eintrichtern.tx: ein- (“in”) + Trichter (“funnel”) + -n, literally “to pour in with a funnel”.

verb:erweichen.tx: From Middle High German erweichen, from Old High German irweihhēn. Equivalent to er- + weich + -en.

verb:ersaufen.tx: From Middle High German *ersūfen, from Old High German irsūfan. Equivalent to er- + saufen.

verb:ersäufen.tx: From Middle High German ersoufen. Compare semantically similar Old High German bisoufen. Causative to ersaufen.

verb:einverleiben.tx: 15th century calque of Latin incorporō, analysable as ein- + verleiben.

verb:erlahmen.tx: From Middle High German erlamen. Equivalent to er- + lahmen.

verb:erzürnen.tx: From Middle High German erzürnen, from Old High German irzurnen. Equivalent to er- + zürnen.

verb:erbieten.tx: From Middle High German erbieten, from Old High German irbiotan, equivalent to er- + bieten.

verb:entmannen.tx: From Middle High German entmannen. Equivalent to ent- (“un-, de-, dis-”) + Mann (“man, male person”) + -en. Compare Dutch ontmannen, English unman.

noun:Entbehrung.tx: 17th century, from entbehren (“to lack, be deprived”) + -ung, probably after Middle Low German entbēringe (15th c.). Compare Dutch ontbering (16th c.).

verb:entfreunden.tx: Calque of English unfriend, equivalent to ent- + Freund + -en.

verb:entwöhnen.tx: From Middle High German entwenen, from Old High German intwennen, from Proto-Germanic *wanjaną (“to accustom”).

verb:entgegensetzen.tx: From Middle High German engegensetzen, from Old High German ingagansezzen. Equivalent to entgegen- + setzen.

verb:erquicken.tx: From Middle High German erquicken, from Old High German irquicken. Equivalent to er- + quick (“lively”) + -en. The simplex quick is Low German, but in the verb the -i- is due to regular lack of a-mutation.

verb:erbeben.tx: From Middle High German erbiben, from Old High German irbibēn. Equivalent to er- + beben.

noun:Endivie.tx: Via a Romance language, compare French endive, Italian indivia, from Late Latin intibus.

phrase:ehrlich gesagt.tx: Literally, “said honestly”. Compare Dutch eerlijk gezegd.

phrase:ein Stein fällt auf den Kopf.tx: Literally, “a stone falls on one’s head”.

verb:erbleichen.tx: From Middle High German erbleichen, from Old High German irbleihhēn. Equivalent to er- + bleichen.

noun:Erbteil.tx: From Middle High German erbeteil, from Old High German [Term?], from Proto-West Germanic [Term?]; compare Old Dutch ervidēl (Dutch erfdeel), Middle Low German ervedēl. By surface analysis, Erbe + Teil.

noun:Evidenz.tx: Borrowed from French évidence or Latin ēvidentia.

noun:Empfängnis.tx: From Middle High German enphencnisse, from Old High German intfangnissa. Equivalent to empfangen + -nis. Originally synonymous with Empfang. In modern German, the two nouns have come to be distinguished semantically.

phrase:ein Vögelchen hat mir gezwitscher.tx: Literally, “a little bird has twittered to me”.

verb:entgelten.tx: From Middle High German entgelten, engelten, from Old High German intgeltan, ingeltan. Equivalent to ent- + gelten.

verb:erbeuten.tx: er- + beuten; see Beute for more.

verb:einbuchten.tx: 19th century, from Low German. Analysable as ein- + Bucht + -en. In Low German, Bucht also means a “pen for livestock”.

verb:entrinnen.tx: From Middle High German entrinnen, from Old High German inttrinnan, intrinnan. Probably related to trennen and abtrünnig. Not related to rinnen, but possibly influenced by it.

verb:eindrücken.tx: From Middle High German īndrucken, from Old High German inthrucken, calque of Latin imprimo; equivalent to ein- + drücken (“to press”).

pron:euresgleichen.tx: eures (genitive case of personal pronoun 2 pl) + gleich (“similar, equal”)

verb:erwählen.tx: From Middle High German erweln, erwellen, from Old High German irwellen. Equivalent to er- + wählen.

verb:erwehren.tx: From Middle High German erwern, from Old High German irwerren, irwerien. Equivalent to er- + wehren.

noun:Eismann.tx: From Eis + Mann. Cognate with Dutch ijsman, English iceman.

phrase:erfroren sind schon viele, aber e.tx: Literally, “many have frozen to death, but no one has yet been stank to death”. erstunken is the past participle of erstinken, but is used in this idiom to mean "killed by stink" by analogy with erfroren.

noun:Engelmacher.tx: From Engel + Macher. Also see Danish englemager and Norwegian Bokmål englemaker.

noun:Einstand.tx: From ein- (“in”) + Stand (“standing, stance”), deverbal from einstehen. The tennis use derives from the idea of “equilibrium”, from the obsolete phrase die Waage steht ein (“the scales are in balance”, literally “the scales stand in”). Contemporary speakers may in this context reinterpret ein as the unrelated numeral for “one”, by analogy with Gleichstand (“tie”, literally “same-stand”).

verb:erkaufen.tx: From Middle High German erkoufen, from Old High German irkoufen, urkoufen. Equivalent to er- + kaufen.

verb:erbitten.tx: From Middle High German erbiten, from Old High German irbitten. Equivalent to er- + bitten. Compare Gothic 𐌿𐍃𐌱𐌹𐌳𐌾𐌰𐌽 (usbidjan).

verb:einreißen.tx: From Middle High German īnrīzen. Equivalent to ein- + reißen.

verb:entgegnen.tx: From Middle High German engegenen, from Old High German ingaganan. By surface analysis, ent- + gegnen.

verb:erwirken.tx: From Middle High German erwürken, from Old High German irwurken. Equivalent to er- + wirken.

verb:entwachsen.tx: From Middle High German entwahsen, unwahsen, from Old High German intwahsan, equivalent to ent- + wachsen. Cognate with Middle Low German entwassen.

noun:Establishment.tx: 19th century, borrowed from English establishment. Doublet of Etablissement.

verb:erhören.tx: From Middle High German erhœren, from Old High German irhōren. Equivalent to er- + hören.

verb:entlohnen.tx: From ent- + lohnen. Compare Old High German itlōnōn (“to reward, compensate, repay”).

verb:einreiben.tx: From Middle High German īnrīben. Equivalent to ein + reiben.

verb:erschlaffen.tx: From Middle High German *erslaffen, from Old High German irslaffēn. Equivalent to er- + schlaffen.

verb:entzücken.tx: From Middle High German enzücken. Equivalent to ent- (“de-, off, away”) + zücken (“to pull”).

verb:erspähen.tx: From Middle High German erspehen, from Old High German irspehōn. Equivalent to er- + spähen.

verb:ereilen.tx: From Middle High German erīlen. Equivalent to er- + eilen.

noun:Eidbruch.tx: From Eid + Bruch. Compare Middle High German eidebreche (“oath-breaking”, adjective), Old English āþbryċe (“oath-breaking, perjury”), whence English oathbreach, Dutch eedbreuk.

noun:Epileptiker.tx: Since the 19th century. Compare Latin epilēpticus, Ancient Greek ἐπιληπτικός (epilēptikós).

phrase:ehe man sichs versieht.tx: From archaic sich (etwas) versehen (“to expect something”).

verb:entschwinden.tx: ent- + schwinden. Compare synonymous Middle High German entswīnen.

noun:Empirismus.tx: empirisch + -ismus, probably under the influence of empirisme.

pt: to can, to preserve food by heating and sealing in a can or jar
noun:Einmachglas.tx: From einmachen (“to can, to preserve food by heating and sealing in a can or jar”) + Glas (“glass”).

verb:einfließen.tx: From Middle High German īnvliezen, from Old High German infliozan. Equivalent to ein- + fließen.

noun:Edamame.tx: Borrowed from Japanese 枝豆 (literally “stem beans”).

noun:Empore.tx: 18th century, from empor (“up”), following earlier Emporkirche. The formation has a Romance feel to it and may be based loosely on Etage or the like.

noun:Engramm.tx: Coined by German evolutionary biologist Richard Semon in 1904 from Ancient Greek ἐν (en, “in”) + γράμμα (grámma, “writing, picture”).

noun:Eisbergsalat.tx: Calque of English iceberg lettuce, Eisberg + Salat

verb:entraten.tx: From Middle High German entrāten, denominally from Middle High German rāt (“counsel, also exemption”), see modern Rat. It is conjugated as if it were a compound ent- + raten.

verb:entschleunigen.tx: ent- + schleunig + -en, newly coined from beschleunigen (“to accelerate”).

verb:einfassen.tx: From Middle High German ī̆nvaʒʒen. By surface analysis, ein- + fassen.

verb:erbeten.tx: From Middle High German *erbeten, from Old High German irbetōn. Equivalent to er- + beten.

noun:Eulenspiegel.tx: From Ulenspiegel (1st half of the 16th century), Middle Low German Ūlenspēgel. Its modern semantics is due to the mischievous nature of Till Eulenspiegel, protagonist of a folklore published in 1515. By surface analysis, Eule + -n- + Spiegel, literally “owl mirror”, an analysis already drawn upon in the original tale.

verb:entehren.tx: From Middle High German entēren, from Old High German intērēn. Equivalent to ent- + Ehre + -en or ent- + ehren.

verb:ermessen.tx: From Middle High German ermezzen, from Old High German irmezzan. Equivalent to er- + messen.

noun:Enthusiast.tx: From Ancient Greek ἐνθουσιαστής (enthousiastḗs, “ecstatic sectarian, zealot”).

verb:erblinden.tx: From Middle High German erblinden, from Old High German irblintēn. Equivalent to er- + blinden.

verb:erschleichen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German erslîchen. By surface analysis, er- + schleichen.

phrase:eine Hand wäscht die andere.tx: Literally, “one hand washes the other”, calque of Latin manus manum lavat.

noun:Einbildungskraft.tx: Calque of Latin vīs imāginātiōnis, Einbildung + -s- + Kraft

verb:einschießen.tx: From Middle High German īnschieȥen, from Old High German inskioȥan. Equivalent to ein- + schießen.

verb:erspüren.tx: From Middle High German erspürn, from Old High German irspurren, irspurien, urspurien. Equivalent to er- + spüren.

noun:Energy-Drink.tx: Unadapted borrowing from English energy drink.

verb:entgegenbringen.tx: From Middle High German *engegenbringen, from Old High German ingaganbringan, ingeginibringan. Equivalent to entgegen- + bringen.

verb:erschwindeln.tx: er- (perfective verb prefix) + schwindeln (“swindle, tell lies”)

noun:Edding.tx: From Edding, a brand of permanent markers, from the family name.

verb:entschlagen.tx: From Middle High German entslahen. Decomposable as ent- + schlagen. Compare Dutch ontslaan.

verb:entgegenstellen.tx: From Middle High German *engegenstellen, from Old High German ingaganstellen. Equivalent to entgegen- + stellen.

noun:Exit-Strategie.tx: Partial calque of English exit strategy.

verb:ersteigen.tx: From Middle High German erstīgen, from Old High German irstīgan. Equivalent to er- + steigen.

noun:Elritze.tx: From Middle High German eldrize, of uncertain origin. Compare Middle High German erlinc (“minnow”).

verb:entwunden.tx: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

verb:erfühlen.tx: From Middle High German ervüelen, from Old High German irfuolen. Equivalent to er- + fühlen.

verb:ertasten.tx: From Middle High German ertasten. Equivalent to er- + tasten.

noun:Einbaum.tx: Ca. 1800, from Bavarian and Alemannic German dialects. By surface analysis, ein (“one”) + Baum (“tree”). Perhaps backformed from the adjective *einbäumig, *einbäumen (“made of one tree”) attested in Old High German einboumig, Middle Low German ênbômen, Old English ānbȳme.

noun:Eierloch.tx: By surface analysis, Ei (“egg”) + -er- + Loch (“hole”). Further origin unknown. Perhaps referencing the vagina or a minced form of Arschloch (“arsehole”). Further possibilities would include perfectly spontaneous origin (for the rhyme and metre) or derivation from an unidentified dialectal term.

noun:Exerzierplatz.tx: From exerzieren (“to drill; to exercise”) + Platz (“place, ground”).

verb:erwünschen.tx: Inherited from Middle High German erwünschen, from Old High German irwunsken. By surface analysis, er- + wünschen.

noun:Equipment.tx: Borrowed from English equipment, from French équipement.

verb:eingraben.tx: From Middle High German ingraben. Equivalent to ein- + graben. Cognate with Bavarian eigråbn, Dutch ingraven, English engrave, ingrave.

verb:entknoten.tx: From Middle High German entknoten. Equivalent to ent- + knoten or ent- + Knoten + -en.

noun:Entwendung.tx: From Middle High German entwendunge. Equivalent to entwenden + -ung.

noun:Ebenmaß.tx: From Middle High German ebenmāz n, ebenmāze f. By surface analysis, eben + Maß.

adj:ebenmäßig.tx: From Middle High German ebenmæzec. By surface analysis, denominal of Ebenmaß. Also analysable as eben + -mäßig.

verb:erschwingen.tx: From Middle High German erswingen, from Old High German irswingan. Equivalent to er- + schwingen.

verb:erflehen.tx: From Middle High German ervlēhen, from Old High German irflehōn, irflēhōn. Equivalent to er- + flehen.

noun:Ehrabschneider.tx: Ehre (“honour”) + abschneiden (“to cut off”) + -er (agent noun suffix)

verb:entgegenstehen.tx: From Middle High German engegenstān, from Old High German ingaganstēn, ingaganstān. Equivalent to entgegen- (“against”) + stehen (“stand”).

verb:entgegengehen.tx: From Middle High German engegengān, ingagengān, from Old High German ingagangān, also ingegingangan, ingagangangan. Equivalent to entgegen- + gehen.

phrase:ein Indianer kennt keinen Schmerz.tx: Literally, “an Indian [i.e. Native American] knows no pain”.

noun:Entstehungsgeschichte.tx: From Entstehung (“creation, origin, development, formation”) + -s- + Geschichte (“history”).

noun:Eigen.tx: From Middle High German eigen, from Old High German eigan, from the neuter of Proto-Germanic *aiganaz.

noun:Einstreu.tx: Back-formation from einstreuen, by surface analysis, ein- + Streu.

noun:Ertragslage.tx: Ertrag (“yield, profit, earnings”) + -s- (“genitival interfix”) + Lage (“situation, position”)

noun:Eigner.tx: From Middle High German eigner, from Old High German eiganari. Equivalent to eigen (“own”) + -er (“agent noun”).

noun:Erste-Hilfe-Kasten.tx: Erste Hilfe (“first aid”) + Kasten (“box, case, cabinet”)

phrase:et kütt wie et kütt.tx: Unadapted borrowing from Ripuarian et kütt wie et kütt (literally “it comes as it comes”).

verb:ertöten.tx: Inherited from Middle High German ertœten, Old High German irtōden. By surface analysis, er- + töten.
